title: Rate Sculptor microbenchmark suite for tokens/sec stability
creator: Aisha Coleman
description: Build a new microbenchmark harness called 'Rate Sculptor' to measure and track tokens-per-second (tokens/sec) and p95 tail latency for our core-serving models under varied load shapes. This suite focuses on realistic token emission patterns (variable sequence lengths, prompt prefix skew, mixed prompt types), cache priming effects, and kernel-selection/quantization permutations. Goals: create a repeatable, low-flakiness benchmark that surfaces regressions early, integrates with existing CI/regression alerts, and provides actionable diffs (delta tokens/sec, delta p95) with root-cause hints (KV cache, batching saturation, kernel fallback).
acceptance_criteria: Benchmark runs end-to-end in CI with deterministic seeding and produces tokens/sec and p95 artifacts
Can compare baseline vs candidate model+runtime and produce a delta report with significance and recommended follow-ups
Integration with regression detector: if p95 regresses >10% or tokens/sec drops >8% the pipeline fails and opens a regression ticket
Support for configurable workload shapes: steady-state, microburst, sawtooth, and multi-tenant interleaving
Expose per-run KV-cache priming controls and kernel-selection flags so we can isolate cause of regressions
test_plan: Local dev harness: lightweight binary that generates workload and emits JSON artifacts
CI integration: nightly and pre-merge smoke checks; full regression runs on release branches
A/B comparator: ingest baseline and candidate outputs and compute tokens/sec, p50, p95, p99, tail-sample distributions
Golden trace reproduction: record traces (latency heatmaps, GPU utilization, batch sizes) for failing regressions
Synthetic-to-production mapping: run subset of production prompts to sanity check benchmark fidelity
observability_specs: Output artifacts written to S3/GCS with job id and seeded random state
Dashboards: per-model tokens/sec trend, p95 trend, regression-alerts, heatmap of sequence-length vs p95
Alerting rules: notify #runtime-regressions and create Linear ticket on threshold breach
Trace linking: include span ids to correlate with Console traces and GPU kernel events
implementation_notes: Prefer Rust harness binary for low overhead and consistent scheduling; Python shim for orchestration and result aggregation
Use deterministic tokenizer seeds and controlled prompt corpus to reduce noise; store corpus snapshots alongside artifacts
Implement warmup phase for KV cache priming and a controlled cold-start test
Parameterize batch sizes and target latency SLOs so we can probe saturation boundaries
Record hardware telemetry (GPU clocks, mem usage, NIC throughput) in parallel with application metrics
rollout_plan: MVP: local harness + nightly CI job for 3 core models (base, med, large) — 2 weeks
Expand: add full model catalog and multi-tenant interleaving patterns — next 3 sprints
Guardrails: add regression-detector integration and automated ticketing before enabling gate on release branch
risks_and_mitigation: Flaky measurements due to infra variance — mitigate by controlled pinning of drivers and repeated runs with statistical tests
High CI cost for full-suite runs — provide fast smoke checks and run full-suite on schedule (nightly/weekly)
False positives from cache effects — require KV-cache controlled runs (cold vs warmed) in comparator
Cross-model comparability: different quantization/kernels can make apples-to-oranges — include metadata and canonicalize where possible
notes: Rate Sculptor name chosen to emphasize shaping the request-rate profile rather than a static load generator
We intentionally separate burst-shape generation from model-invocation layer so we can reuse the same shapes across dedicated/private deployments
Keep artifacts small: compress trace bundles and keep recent 30 runs hot while archiving older ones
